Welcome to a space where we get to explore what it really means to accept ourselves, flaws and all.
You ever wonder how someone finds the courage to embrace who they are, even when it feels like the world doesn't quite understand them?
Well, together, we're about to dive into a story that’s as real as it gets—full of vulnerability, resilience, and those tiny sparks of hope that keep us going.
In Jonathan Van Ness’s Over the Top: A Raw Journey to Self-Love, we’ll walk alongside someone who’s navigated the ups and downs of growing up different—feeling shame, wrestling with trauma, and longing to belong.
What’s truly inspiring is how Jonathan’s journey transforms pain into laughter, scars into strength, and self-doubt into a celebration of uniqueness.
Through honest reflections and stories that don’t shy away from the tough stuff, you’ll find moments that hit close to home—because the path to loving yourself is both deeply personal and something we all share.
As we step into this journey together, let’s get ready to challenge old beliefs, find comfort in vulnerability, and maybe, just maybe, see our own stories reflected in Jonathan’s.
So, are you ready to discover what it means to love yourself, out loud and unapologetically?
Let’s begin.

Chapter 1. Early Years: Searching for Belonging and Understanding.
You know, childhood can feel a bit like trying to solve a puzzle when you’re missing a few key pieces—especially if, deep down, you’ve always known you don’t quite fit the mold everyone expects.
Picture a small Midwestern town. There’s the steady beat of family routines, school bells, and familiar faces around every corner. But underneath all that, there’s a gentle hum—a constant reminder that you’re not quite like everyone else, and maybe the world wants you to be a little more... ordinary.
This child—full of energy and life—lights up whenever dance, gymnastics, or a little bit of sparkle is involved. But here’s the thing: the world around doesn’t always know what to do with that kind of passion.
Instead of applause, there are those sideways glances, the whispers you pretend not to hear, and that quiet pressure to just blend in. The playground, which should be a place for giggles and games, sometimes turns into a stage for feeling left out. And even the classroom—supposed to be a safe space for learning—can feel like a daily struggle for acceptance.
Now, home is filled with love, but it’s complicated. Family members, each wrestling with their own hopes and worries, try to offer support. But sometimes their words just don’t quite land right.
There’s this deep longing—to truly be seen and cherished, just as you are. Early on, you learn that being different isn’t always easy. Sometimes, even the people who love you most can’t fully understand what you’re feeling inside.
As those first years start to fade and adolescence creeps in, that feeling of being on the outside looking in only grows stronger. School gets trickier—social circles tighten, and the rules for fitting in seem more confusing than ever.
You want to belong, but you’re also pulled by the urge to be real, to be authentic. There are bright moments: maybe a teacher who celebrates your creativity, a friend who confides in you, or a performance that actually earns applause.
But too often, those moments get overshadowed by the sting of rejection, or that quiet ache of loneliness that just won’t go away.
During these years, seeds of self-doubt start to take root. It’s easy to start believing that being yourself is risky.
But here’s something important: even in the midst of all that uncertainty, a quiet resilience starts to grow. There’s a determination to find your place in this world—even if it means blazing your own trail.
And often, the journey toward self-acceptance doesn’t start with some grand, dramatic moment.
It begins with small acts of courage—maybe wearing that favorite outfit, raising your hand in class, or daring to dream about a life that’s bigger than what you’ve always known.
When you look back on those early struggles, it becomes clearer—they’re not just obstacles. They’re the building blocks for something much greater.
The pain of not fitting in makes the longing for real connection that much sharper. Being misunderstood? It plants the seeds of deep empathy for others. And every day you survive, even when it’s tough, that’s a victory in itself.

Chapter 2: Facing Trauma and the Long Road to Healing
As the years go by, life has a way of throwing challenges our way—sometimes quietly, sometimes with a force that leaves us breathless.
For some, trauma sneaks in, barely noticeable at first, almost blending into the background of everyday life. For others, it crashes in, leaving marks that just won’t fade. In this story, trauma comes in many shapes—bullying, loss, and sometimes, the painful reality of abuse.
The pain from these moments? It’s tough to describe. There’s confusion—wondering how you’re supposed to process what happened. There’s shame, sticking to every memory, and that fear of being judged or brushed aside.
People so often say, “Just move on,” or, “Be strong,” but real healing doesn’t work like that. It’s never a straight path. Instead, it’s messy, unpredictable, and at times, it can feel incredibly lonely.
After trauma, coping almost becomes a way of life. Some people lean on humor, letting laughter protect them from the darkness. Others throw themselves into work, relationships, or even substances—anything to numb that overwhelming pain.
The search for relief can be exhausting and winding. Still, there are glimmers of hope—a friend who listens, a therapist who cares, or a moment when things start to make sense. But let’s be honest, setbacks happen, and progress can feel painfully slow.
What’s important to remember is that the journey through trauma is made up of small victories. Maybe it’s finally being able to name the pain, or finding the courage to actually say it out loud.
Asking for help, trusting someone with your truth—that’s huge. And little by little, the weight of shame begins to lift. In its place, there’s a growing sense of self-worth, and a feeling that, maybe, you have some control over your own story.
Healing isn’t about wiping the slate clean or erasing the past. It’s about weaving those tough experiences into your life’s story. The scars? They’re still there, but they don’t have the last word anymore.
There’s a new understanding: being vulnerable isn’t a weakness—it’s actually a sign of real strength. By sharing your truth and refusing to hide, you start to reclaim your power and build a new sense of self.
And let’s not forget the power of support systems. Friends, family, and professionals—they become your anchors, offering encouragement, guidance, and a safe place to heal.
Community is a lifeline. It reminds survivors that they’re not alone. Through connection, the isolation that trauma brings starts to fade, making room for belonging and hope.

Chapter 3: The Struggle with Addiction and the Search for Control.
You know, adulthood opens up a whole new world of freedom—fresh choices, endless possibilities. But it also brings its own set of temptations and pressures, doesn’t it? For someone who’s spent years feeling out of place, it’s easy to see why the idea of escape can be so appealing. Substances might seem like a quick fix—a way to turn down the volume on anxiety, self-doubt, or that relentless need to always perform. In the beginning, that relief can feel almost magical. It’s a chance to finally quiet the noise and just feel comfortable in your own skin, even if it’s only for a moment.
But here’s where it gets tricky. Addiction is clever. What starts out as a way to cope can quickly become a trap. The cycle of using and then regretting tightens its grip, making it harder and harder to break free. Relationships start to suffer, work can get shaky, and you might begin to lose sight of who you really are. And the shame that comes with feeling out of control? That just adds another layer of pain, often fueling the very habits you’re trying to escape.
Still, there are those moments of clarity—times when you can’t ignore the consequences anymore. Maybe it’s a missed opportunity, a promise you couldn’t keep, or a scary health wake-up call. These moments feel terrifying, but they’re also crucial. They force you to face the truth: something’s got to change.
Recovery, though, isn’t just one big decision. It’s a series of choices, made day after day. It takes real honesty, humility, and the courage to start fresh. You lean on support groups, therapy, and the steady presence of folks who care about you. These become the scaffolding for a brand new life. Sure, there are setbacks—moments of doubt, and always, that temptation to slip back into old habits. But with every step forward, even the small ones, addiction’s hold starts to loosen.
What’s really powerful is what you discover along the way. Addiction isn’t a sign of weakness or some moral failure—it’s a response to pain. It grows in secrecy and shame, but loses its power when you bring it into the open and connect with others. Recovery isn’t just about quitting; it’s about learning self-compassion—forgiving yourself, accepting your imperfections, and celebrating progress, no matter how tiny.
Over time, something shifts. The urge to escape fades, replaced by a real desire to be present. The world, once overwhelming, starts to feel manageable. You find a new sense of agency—a belief that you really can live life on your own terms. And even though the struggle with addiction is tough, it leaves you with wisdom and empathy—a reminder that everyone’s got battles no one else can see.

prosody.p: Chapter 4: Embracing Identity and Living Authentically.

You know, the journey to truly accepting yourself can feel like a long, winding road. Everywhere you look, the world throws out ideas about how you should look, act, or even love. And if you happen to walk a path that doesn’t fit the mainstream mold, those messages can sting even more. The pressure to fit in? It’s non-stop. And sometimes, just being yourself can seem like the hardest thing in the world.

But there comes a moment—a tipping point—when you just can’t hide anymore. The need to live honestly, to be seen for who you are, starts to outweigh the fear of what others might think. Coming out isn’t just one big announcement; it’s a bunch of conversations, each one a little leap of faith. Sometimes you’re met with open arms, other times with confusion or even pushback. Still, with every truth you share, the weight you’ve been carrying gets a little lighter.

Living authentically means embracing every part of who you are—the strengths, the flaws, the highs, and even the tough moments. It’s about deciding not to shrink back or apologize for simply existing. Sure, there will be bumps along the way—moments when old worries creep back in. But there’s also an incredible sense of freedom that grows, a real joy in being able to just show up as yourself.

And here’s where community becomes so important. Finding people who’ve walked similar paths makes all the difference. Suddenly, you have a place where you belong—where shared laughter, support, and celebration lift you up. You start to realize: there’s no single right way to be. Everyone’s journey is their own.

When you embrace your identity, you’re also taking on a responsibility—not just to yourself, but to others. Living openly pushes past stereotypes and breaks down old barriers. It gives hope to anyone still feeling stuck in the shadows, proof that it’s possible to live authentically. The road ahead will bring new challenges and new chances to grow. But the foundation is laid: living your truth, loving who you are, and building a life on honesty and acceptance. That’s what matters most.

Chapter 5: Navigating Stigma and Finding Power in Vulnerability.
Some challenges feel deeply personal, while others are shaped by the world’s ignorance and fear. If you live with a chronic condition—especially one that’s surrounded by stigma—you know it takes a whole different kind of courage.
The diagnosis often arrives out of nowhere. Suddenly, you’re hit with a wave of fear, shame, and uncertainty. Your mind starts racing. You wonder about your health, your future, and maybe most of all—how will people react if they find out?
Carrying this secret can feel like dragging around a heavy weight. There’s this constant calculation running through your head: Who do you tell? How much do you share? Is it worth the risk?
The fear of rejection is real, and the pain of being misunderstood can be almost too much. But here’s something to pay attention to: hiding the truth only makes that sense of isolation grow stronger.
Over time, choosing to live openly becomes its own kind of rebellion. It’s a way of saying, “I won’t let shame decide how I live.” At first, you might share your truth with just a few trusted friends. Maybe, eventually, you tell more people.
The response? It’s a mixed bag. Some people show up with unconditional support, while others might back away. But you’ll notice that being vulnerable—really letting yourself be seen—opens up space for connection, for genuine understanding, and even for healing.
Living with a stigmatized condition is a daily act of resilience. You’re moving through a world that’s often uninformed, sometimes even hostile, and not always compassionate.
But here’s the thing: you also discover a strength inside yourself that you maybe never knew was there. This experience, as hard as it is, can help you find empathy for others—connecting you to people fighting their own battles.
So if you’re navigating stigma, remember: vulnerability isn’t weakness. It’s power. And every time you share your truth, you make it a little easier for someone else to do the same.

Chapter 6: The Power of Community and Chosen Family
You know, there’s this moment that happens on every journey—a shift from just wanting to fit in, to actually feeling seen for who you are. Maybe you’ve felt it too. For a lot of us, the family we’re born into can only bring us so far on that path. The rest? That’s where we find our people—the ones who just get us, who laugh at our weird jokes, and stick around when life gets hard. Picture this: in the heart of a noisy city, someone steps into a room buzzing with music and laughter. Every face is new, but the vibe couldn’t be clearer—acceptance, warmth, and, honestly, a little bit of magic. It’s a gathering of folks who’ve all, at some point, felt like outsiders. But here? Differences aren’t just accepted—they’re treasured. There’s this freedom in the air, like you can finally relax, let your guard down, and just breathe. The real magic of chosen family comes from what you share together. It’s those late-night talks about dreams and disappointments, the spontaneous dance parties that pop up in tiny apartments, and the quiet support when the world outside feels overwhelming. Sure, it’s not always perfect—people argue, misunderstandings happen. But what matters is, you keep showing up for each other. Pretty soon, you realize that community isn’t just about living near someone or liking the same things. It’s about being willing to witness each other’s lives, to offer comfort without judgment, and to celebrate even the tiniest wins. In these circles, the old scars from rejection start to fade. You don’t have to hide anymore. Instead, you begin to feel proud of your own story. For many of us, chosen family becomes a lifeline. When the world turns harsh, these are the people who remind you how much you matter. When the doubts creep in, they help you see your own strength. And here’s the most important thing: we’re not meant to do this alone. Real connection isn’t just something nice to have—it’s what keeps us going. It’s resilience. It’s hope.

Chapter 7: Finding Purpose Through Passion and Service.
When the dust finally settles after a long season of just trying to survive, a new question quietly rises up: what now? You know, for so long, life was all about getting through the day—finding safety, searching for acceptance, working on healing. But once you’ve built that steady foundation, something shifts. Suddenly, there’s space to dream again. And that gentle tug you feel? That’s the search for purpose, inviting you to step into something bigger.
For some people, purpose starts with creativity. There’s this special kind of joy that comes from making things—like art, music, or stories—that capture both the mess and the beauty of real life. Picture someone in a sunlit studio, completely lost in the rhythm of painting. The way those colors swirl across the canvas, it’s almost like they’re echoing all the twists and turns of their own journey. Creating isn’t just about making something pretty—it’s a way to process pain, celebrate joy, and connect with others who might be feeling the same way.
For others, purpose is all about service. After years of feeling invisible, there’s this strong desire to help someone else feel seen. Maybe it’s volunteering at a youth center, or mentoring someone who’s just starting out, or even just really listening to a friend who needs it. These small acts of kindness? They ripple outward, making a difference in ways you might not even notice at first, but they matter—a lot.
And here’s something interesting: passion and service aren’t really separate paths. In fact, they’re deeply connected. The things that spark your energy—those passions—are often the very things that can help other people, too. Sharing your story, teaching what you know, offering a shoulder to lean on... these are all ways you can turn pain into purpose.
There’s a quiet satisfaction that comes with realizing your struggles weren’t wasted. Every tough moment, every doubt, it all becomes fuel for empathy and action. Your own journey toward self-love doesn’t just stop with you—it spreads out, touches other lives, and builds a legacy of hope.

Chapter 8: Navigating Success, Setbacks, and the Spotlight.
You know, when success finally shows up, it’s almost never that neat, storybook moment we dream about. If you’ve spent years fighting just to be seen, that recognition can feel like a wild mix of excitement and fear.
Suddenly, you’re in the spotlight. There are doors opening, sure, but now there’s a new kind of pressure too. Every little thing you say or do? It feels like it’s under a microscope, and even the smallest slip-up can get blown way out of proportion.
With all those eyes watching, old doubts and insecurities have a funny way of sneaking back in. You might catch yourself wanting to shrink back, to stick to what’s safe, or to become the version of yourself you think everyone wants. But here’s something worth remembering—the lessons from your journey are still with you. Staying true to who you are isn’t optional. The price you pay for hiding is just too steep.
Of course, there are moments that make it all worthwhile—like a standing ovation, or when a stranger reaches out with a message that hits you right in the heart. Maybe it’s seeing your work connect with people in ways you never imagined. Those are the moments reminding you that this journey matters, and that telling your truth really can make a difference.
But setbacks are part of the deal too. There’s criticism that can really sting, chances that slip through your fingers, and just the sheer exhaustion of always having to be “on.”
Pretty soon, you realize that success isn’t a finish line you cross. It’s more like an ongoing process—a commitment to show up, again and again, even when it’s tough. It’s learning how to accept praise without letting it define you, and facing criticism without letting it tear you down.
The real victory? It isn’t in the applause. It’s in that steady, quiet confidence that comes from knowing you’re already enough, just as you are.
Through all of it, the people who stand beside you—your community, your chosen family—they’re everything. They’re the ones who keep you grounded, who remind you what really matters, and who celebrate the person you truly are, not just your public persona.
With them by your side, you can navigate all those highs and lows with a bit more grace, and a whole lot more resilience.

Let’s talk about something that’s both simple and surprisingly hard—self-love.
Chapter Nine: The Ongoing Practice of Self-Love.
Self-love isn’t some final destination you cross off your list. It’s more like a daily practice—a bunch of small choices you make, especially in those quiet moments when nobody else is around.
Have you ever caught yourself thinking, “If I just heal this one thing, I’ll finally feel confident?” I get it. It’s easy to picture healing as a single, life-changing event, and confidence as something that magically shows up fully formed. But real life? It’s messier, and honestly, a lot more beautiful.
There will be days when those old doubts creep back in. Maybe you look in the mirror and only see your flaws. Or the world just feels... indifferent. On days like these, self-love is almost rebellious. It’s choosing not to believe the worst about yourself.
Sometimes, it’s as simple as playing your favorite song on repeat, taking a walk outside, or cooking a meal with extra care. These little rituals—they might seem ordinary, but they become your anchors.
Self-love also means drawing boundaries. It’s okay to say no to things that drain you or make you feel small. And sometimes, it’s about reaching out, admitting you can’t do it all by yourself. There’s a quiet strength in that honesty—a reminder that real strength isn’t about never needing anyone, but about knowing when to ask for help.
This journey is ongoing. You’ll hit setbacks. There will be disappointments and days when it feels like you’re not making any progress at all. But don’t forget, there are breakthroughs too—those flashes of clarity, bursts of real joy, and the quiet pride that comes from living true to your values.
Over time, self-love becomes less about big, dramatic gestures, and more about showing up for yourself, day after day. It’s forgiving yourself, trying again, and holding onto the belief that you’re worthy of kindness—especially your own.
If there’s one thing to remember, it’s this: self-love isn’t about being perfect. It’s about being patient, gentle, and willing to start over, as many times as it takes.

Chapter 10: Sharing the Story and Inspiring Others.
Eventually, your journey reaches a point where it starts to reach outward. All the pain you’ve carried, the healing you’ve worked so hard for, and every bit of wisdom you’ve gathered—these aren’t just your own milestones. They’re gifts, meant to be shared.
There’s something powerful about telling your truth. When you let people see the messy, complicated, and honestly beautiful reality of living authentically, it does more than just help you—it creates connection.
Picture this: a packed auditorium, and someone steps up to the microphone. Their heart’s pounding. The story they share isn’t polished or perfect—it’s real. There are flashes of fear, moments of hope. As they speak, you can almost feel the weight lifting—a release of shame, and a moment of reclaiming their own power.
You look around and notice the audience. Some people have tears in their eyes, others are nodding, completely understanding. Suddenly, strangers don’t feel so far apart. In that moment, the story becomes a bridge, connecting lives that may have never crossed paths.
Now, not everyone will get it. Some might judge, or even turn away. But for the people who are struggling—those who feel completely alone in their pain—your story can be a lifeline. It’s proof that surviving is possible, and that real joy can actually exist on the other side of suffering.
And here’s something to remember: sharing isn’t just about helping others. It’s also for you. It’s a way to honor everything you’ve been through, to find meaning in the mess. It’s a reminder that vulnerability isn’t a weakness—it’s a real source of strength.
No matter how ordinary or extraordinary your story might seem, it has the power to heal. Both for you, and for someone who desperately needs to hear it.

As we wrap up, just take a moment to recognize how far you’ve come on this journey of self-love. It’s not always easy, and it’s definitely not a straight line. There are ups and downs, setbacks, and little victories along the way—but every step you take matters.
Here’s what really stands out: Self-love isn’t something you just arrive at—it’s something you practice, day in and day out. You don’t have to get it perfect. What counts is that you keep showing up for yourself, even on the tough days.
Leaning on community—your chosen family, your friends—can be such a powerful source of healing. And when you let yourself be vulnerable, even if it feels scary, you open the door to deeper connections and real growth.
Sometimes, the hardest moments end up giving us purpose. When you reach out to help someone else, you can turn pain into hope, both for them and for yourself.
And don’t forget—the simple act of sharing your story matters. You never know who you might inspire, or how much strength you’ll find in your own voice.
So, if you’re feeling unsure, just remember: You don’t have to have all the answers to get started. The path to loving yourself keeps unfolding, and it’s totally okay to stumble now and then. Just keep moving forward, keep reaching out, and keep believing that you’re enough—exactly as you are.
The world needs your light, your story, and your presence. So take a deep breath, trust where you’re headed, and know you’re never alone on this journey. Every small act of self-kindness, every honest moment, is another step towards a life that’s not just about getting by, but about truly living.
